fields.summary: M-00 Microbiology Module Parent (spec, glossary, RBAC, phase plan)
fields.description:
## Overview

Parent / spine + **umbrella** for the Microbiology / AMR Module. Read this spec first. Anchors the _17-epic M-_ bundle\* (M-00 through M-15 plus M-NFR) with the cross-cutting glossary, RBAC matrix, data-model overview, phase plan, and the v1.1 → v2 diff map. There is no Initiative level above this epic; every module epic _Relates_ to it. **Owner: Piotr Mankowski.**

## The 17 epics

* **Foundations:** OGC-786 M-01 Reference data · OGC-784 M-12 Reagent linkage · OGC-788 M-08 Macro library · OGC-783 M-NFR · OGC-782 M-00 (this)
* **Catalog:** OGC-787 M-02 Breakpoints (CLSI/EUCAST **+ WHO-TB**)
* **Case hub:** OGC-790 M-04 Case Workbench · **OGC-901 M-14 Mycobacteriology/TB** (profile of M-04)
* **Operational:** OGC-789 M-03 Order-entry hook · OGC-791 M-05 AST entry · OGC-785 M-11 Critical notify
* **Review/Worklist:** OGC-792 M-07 Worklists · OGC-793 M-06 Expert rules
* **Surveillance/Reporting:** OGC-794 M-09 WHONET · **OGC-900 M-13 Antibiogram** · **OGC-918 M-15 GLASS via consolidated FHIR (last)** · OGC-795 M-10 Hub subscription

Dependency graph: `amr-micro-dependency-graph.svg` (17 epics; build order + key deps).

## Cross-cutting decisions (landed across the bundle)

* **Workflow routing:** the ordered test carries a `workflow_type` (BACTERIOLOGY vs MYCOBACTERIOLOGY_TB) set on the Test Catalog (**OGC-925**); the M-03 resolver instantiates the matching Case profile, breakpoint family, Method, and WHONET flavor. UNASSIGNED fallback + tech **Change workflow** (**OGC-926**).
* **Case keying:** `micro_case` keyed to **SampleItem × workflow_type** (not 1:1 with Sample) — one specimen can hold a bacterial _and_ a TB Case sharing the SampleItem (build stories OGC-820/843 re-keyed).
* **Reuse, don't rebuild:** M-09 extends the **existing** OpenELIS WHONET export; M-11 reuses the **existing** notifications/alerts dashboard + `TestNotificationService`; TB DST reuses `micro_ast_run`; Timeline reuses History/Note.
* **Inline, not modal** (Principle 3) for M-06 / M-11 bench surfaces.

## Scope

**MVP-1A** — doc only; lock M-00 before sprint 1. Contents: glossary, data-model overview, RBAC matrix across all modules, phase plan (MVP-1A → 1A+ → 1B → Phase 2), out-of-scope, v1.1 → v2 diff map, cross-cutting constraints (single-tenancy, sidenav submenus, Carbon for React, reuse-existing-elements, i18n `module.surface.element`).

## Now in scope (were previously out)

**Mycobacteriology/TB (M-14)**, **Antibiogram (M-13)**, and **GLASS reporting (M-15, via consolidated FHIR)** are now planned modules (satisfy procurement requirement #8). Cross-lab _aggregation_ stays outside OE (single-tenancy); each lab pushes its own data.

## Source documents

* `m-00-micro-module-parent.md`; narrative `amr-micro-narrative.md` (**v2.1**), published to Confluence: \[Microbiology Module — Workflow Walk-through (for developers)|https://uwdigi.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/oeg/pages/1315209256\]

## Sizing

\~4 story points (doc-only epic: lock M-00, publish glossary, RBAC sign-off). Full bundle ≈ 17 epics / \~578 story points (see `amr-micro-backlog.md`).

## Supersedes

OGC-293 — closed as superseded. This umbrella replaces the original AMR monolith with the 17-epic M-\* bundle.

* NFR-08 Security & access control (server-side permission checks; existing OE session auth)
* NFR-09 Browser support (latest 2 versions of Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari)

fields.summary: M-01 AMR Reference Data (Organism, Antibiotic, AST Panel, Culture Protocol masters)
fields.description:
## Overview

Four reference-data vocabularies that drive the Micro workflow, all under `Admin → Microbiology Reference Data` (sidenav submenus, not in-page tabs):

* **Organism Master** — every organism the lab can identify, with WHONET codes for surveillance, organism groups for rule application, intrinsic resistances, default AST panel.
* **Antibiotic Master** — every antibiotic the lab can test, with WHONET codes and class taxonomy.
* **AST Panels** — which antibiotics get tested against which organism × specimen combinations, with tier ordering for cascade reporting.
* **Culture Protocols** — recipe per specimen type: media, incubation time, temperature, atmosphere.

Per crosswalk Q6: Organism Master is a greenfield master, but it's referenced by micro Tests via the existing Test Catalog coded-result-vocabulary mechanism (no new write pipeline; reuses existing infrastructure).

## Scope

Three additional vocabulary augmentations of existing OE entities (per crosswalk Q7):

* Specimen Type — add `whonet_code` field to existing Sample Type vocabulary

* Department — add `whonet_code` field to existing dept vocabulary

fields.summary: M-08 Macro Library (cross-cutting typing shortcuts; .code → expanded text)
fields.description:
## Outcome

Laboratory staff can insert approved, reusable phrases into narrative fields quickly and consistently. An authorized administrator maintains the shared phrase library. The inserted phrase remains ordinary editable text in the laboratory record.

Microbiology is the first consumer, but the user capability is cross-cutting and may later be used in other laboratory disciplines.

## M1 - Managed phrase workflow

### Laboratory user

* Typing a dot-prefixed shortcut or choosing a matching suggestion shows only active phrases applicable to the current field.
* Keyboard and pointer selection replace only the shortcut and preserve surrounding text.
* The expanded phrase remains editable and is what the existing workflow saves.
* Unknown, incomplete, inactive, or out-of-context shortcuts remain unchanged.
* Suggestions are understandable to screen-reader users, keyboard complete, and usable at desktop and mobile widths.
* Initial supported fields are culture activity notes, microbiology clinical history, and antibiotic exposure.

### Laboratory administrator

* Authorized users can create, find, update, activate, and deactivate shared phrases.
* Phrase codes are unique, dot-prefixed, and paired with non-empty phrase text and at least one supported field context.
* Search, filter, sort, pagination, and active editing state can be restored from a bookmarked URL.
* Changes are attributable to the authenticated administrator and are available to a subsequently loaded supported form.
* Deactivation prevents new use without altering text already saved in laboratory records.
* Non-administrators can use eligible phrases but cannot change the library.

## M2 - Reviewed package and broader administration

* OpenELIS-provided phrases must have an exact source, version, content set, and named clinical approval before release.
* Adopting or restoring a reviewed package must preserve local phrases and report collisions instead of silently overwriting them.
* Administrators can export the effective library and use explicit bulk actions.
* Additional narrative fields can adopt the same user interaction after their workflow intent is approved.

## Acceptance guardrails

* Draft mockups and tickets describe workflow intent, not binding routes, tables, services, caches, component names, permission constants, or other technical design.
* No clinical phrase is shipped solely because it appears in a draft mock.
* Implementation details, repository state, migrations, API decisions, fixtures, and test strategy belong in the linked engineering spec and pull requests.

## References

* Product and engineering spec: https://github.com/DIGI-UW/OpenELIS-Global-2/tree/spec/788-ogc-788-macro-library/specs/788-ogc-788-macro-library
* Spec PR: https://github.com/DIGI-UW/OpenELIS-Global-2/pull/3986
* M1 implementation PR: https://github.com/DIGI-UW/OpenELIS-Global-2/pull/3990
* M-08 workflow intent: https://digi-uw.github.io/openelis-work/#/microbiology/m-08-macro-library
* Microbiology workflow walkthrough: https://uwdigi.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/oeg/pages/1315209256

fields.summary: M-06 Expert Rules Engine (MRSA, D-test, ESBL, cascade, intrinsic verification)
fields.description:
## Overview

Configurable rules engine that runs against AST Run state changes and produces flags and overrides. Phase 1B feature; Phase 1A ships with manual expert review (tech and supervisor apply rules manually via overrides in M-05).

Five rule types:

* **Resistance phenotype inference** — e.g., S. aureus oxacillin-R → MRSA → all beta-lactams forced to R (patient-safety; auto-apply)
* **D-test required** — S. aureus erythromycin-R + clindamycin-S → flag for D-test
* **ESBL screen / confirmation** — Enterobacterales with 3GC resistance → flag → tech runs phenotypic confirmation → over-ride
* **Cascade reporting** — urine E. coli first-line all-R → unlock second-tier panel for reporting
* **Intrinsic resistance verification** — flag AST results contradicting an organism's known intrinsic resistance

## Scope

**Phase 1B** — full engine + 5 built-in rules. MVP-1A and 1A+ use manual overrides via M-05.

* `expert_rule_definition` + `expert_rule_definition_version` + `expert_rule_flag` schema
* JSON-driven rule evaluator
* 5 built-in rules with sensible defaults
* Expert Review section in M-04 Case Detail
* Expert Review Decision modal with decision options + macro-enabled justification
* Phenotype flags on Isolate (`micro_isolate_phenotype` table; surfaced in WHONET export columns)
* Re-evaluation rules per crosswalk Q4 Rule 2 (snapshot rule version; no auto re-run on reidentification)
* Rule admin page (list + version history)
* Custom rule editor (basic JSON paste-in; full UI Phase 2)

## Source documents

fields.summary: M-09 WHONET Export (surveillance export to national reference lab)
fields.description:
## Overview

Generate WHONET-format CSV/TXT files from finalized Cases for submission to the country's national reference lab (which aggregates from multiple labs and produces the country's GLASS submission). Plus the admin surface for code mapping (organism, antibiotic, specimen, origin, patient type, phenotype) to WHONET codes.

**GLASS direct submission is out of scope** — OpenELIS is single-tenant per deployment (`project_no_multitenancy`); aggregation across labs happens centrally outside OE.

## Scope

**Phase 1B** — surveillance is not in MVP.

* `whonet_export_run` audit schema
* WHONET Mapping admin — 8 sidenav sub-pages (Organisms, Antibiotics, Specimens, Origins, Patient Types, Departments, Breakpoint Standards, Phenotypes)
* Export Generator UI — date range, filters (specimen / organism / origin / significance), dedup parameters (6 configurable, default WHO GLASS-aligned), output format (WHONET CSV / TXT)
* Dedup algorithm — first-isolate per patient per organism per 7 days (configurable window, basis, scope, significance handling)
* Validation pass (errors block; warnings advisory; inline "Map now" for unmapped codes)
* WHONET file generation with full column set (demographic, specimen, organism, AST results per multi-method suffix, phenotype flags from M-06, comment/metadata)
* Lab profile (.wri or current format) packaging for first-time bootstrap to national reference lab
* File naming template: `{COUNTRY}_{LAB}_{YYYY-MM-DD}_to_{YYYY-MM-DD}.csv`
* Preview UI (sample rows + summary)
* Export history page with re-download
* AST Worklist quick action ("Export to WHONET")
* Single Case export from Case Detail
* Phenotype flag column writer (reads from M-06 phenotype tags)
* Scheduled export (Phase 2): cron + SFTP / email delivery

## Source documents

fields.summary: M-10 Hub Subscription — RETIRED (folded into Catalog Subscription)
fields.description:
## Overview

Unifies what was previously split between AMR Configuration §9 (Hub for organism/antibiotic/AST Panel updates) and WHONET Integration §2.3 (Import Hub for WHONET codes). One admin page, one mechanism, four data domains.

fields.description:
## Overview

Cumulative antibiogram reporting for the Microbiology Module — a periodic report giving the **percentage of isolates of an organism that are susceptible (%S) to each antibiotic** over a time window, used to guide empiric therapy. Built per **CLSI M39** methodology from finalized AST data.

This is a **reporting** module: it owns no clinical workflow and introduces no new result-capture entities. It reads finalized `micro_ast_run` results (M-05) and reuses the **first-isolate-per-patient deduplication** already designed for WHONET export (M-09) so the antibiogram is not skewed by repeat isolates from the same patient.

## Scope

**Phase 2** — surveillance/reporting, after the case + AST + WHONET foundation.

* New reporting route `/reports/antibiogram` (sidenav under Reports).
* Selection controls: organism (or organism group), date range, specimen filter, patient-origin filter (inpatient/outpatient/ICU), minimum-isolate threshold (CLSI M39 recommends ≥30 isolates; suppress or footnote below threshold).
* First-isolate dedup (reuse M-09 algorithm: first isolate per patient per organism per configurable window).
* Cumulative %S matrix: organisms (rows) × antibiotics (columns), each cell = %S + n; color coding by %S band; intrinsic-resistance and not-tested cells blanked, not zeroed.
* Footnotes: total isolates, dedup basis, breakpoint standard/version used, suppression notes for under-threshold cells.
* Export: PDF (formatted report) + CSV (raw matrix). No new data store — derived on demand from AST results.
* TB note: a TB-specific cumulative resistance summary (MTB-complex %R by drug) is produced through M-14 + WHONET-TB, not this bacterial antibiogram surface.

## Source documents

* `m-13-antibiogram.md` (consolidated FRS, v2.0)
* Mockup: `m-13-antibiogram-prototype.html`

## Reuse / consumers

* **Reads** M-05 finalized AST results + M-02 breakpoint standard snapshot (for the footnote).
* **Reuses** M-09's first-isolate dedup concept (CLSI M39 / WHO M-AMR-9 first-isolate rule).
* Feeds the Management Dashboard antibiogram heatmap (OGC-897) as a shared query source.

## Sizing

\~21 story points (reporting module; no new workflow entities). Sub-stories: route + selection UI; dedup reuse wiring; %S matrix builder + color bands; threshold suppression + footnotes; PDF export; CSV export.

## Status

One of the M-\* bundle epics. /specify + mockup complete; awaiting sprint decomposition into child Stories.

fields.summary: M-14 Mycobacteriology / TB (AFB smear, culture, species ID, phenotypic DST + molecular)
fields.description:
## Overview

The Mycobacteriology / TB workflow. **M-14 is a TB _profile_ of the M-04 Case Workbench, not a second workbench** — it reuses the same Case / Isolate / AST-Run shapes, the same shared Worklist (M-07), the same Timeline (History/Note), and the same release/report machinery, instantiated with a TB lifecycle and TB-specific sections. The "which workflow" decision is made by the ordered test's `workflow_type = MYCOBACTERIOLOGY_TB` (M-03 §2.1a / M-00), so a tech never chooses bacterial-vs-TB by hand.

TB differs from bacteriology in four ways the profile captures:

* **AFB smear** — Ziehl-Neelsen / auramine microscopy with WHO/IUATLD grading (neg, scanty, 1+, 2+, 3+).
* **Long culture** — MGIT liquid / Löwenstein-Jensen solid, weeks-long incubation; extended Timeline.
* **Species ID** — _M. tuberculosis_ complex vs NTM.
* **DST against WHO critical concentrations** — phenotypic DST reports **R/S at a single critical concentration** (not the S/I/R clinical-MIC ladder), plus **molecular** resistance (GeneXpert MTB/RIF Ultra, line probe assays) reported as genotypic flags. Derives MDR / pre-XDR / XDR categories.

## Scope

**Phase 2** — after the bacterial case + AST + breakpoint + WHONET foundation is shipped.

* `workflow_type = MYCOBACTERIOLOGY_TB` wiring on the M-03 trigger resolver → TB Case profile.
* New entities: `tb_smear` (AFB grade + method) and `tb_molecular_result` (assay, target, genotypic resistance flags). Phenotypic DST **reuses** `micro_ast_run` with `interpretation_method = CRITICAL_CONCENTRATION` against WHO-TB breakpoints (M-02 extension), not a new run table.
* TB Case sections: Smear, Culture (MGIT/LJ with day-N tracking), Species ID, Phenotypic DST, Molecular results, staged interim reports (smear → culture → ID → DST as each lands).
* MDR / pre-XDR / XDR derivation from combined phenotypic + molecular results.
* Critical-result handling for RIF-resistant / MDR detection (reuse M-11).
* Feeds WHONET-TB export (M-09 §4.5 extension) and the consolidated-FHIR/GLASS path (separate, last).

## Source documents

* `m-14-mycobacteriology-tb.md` (consolidated FRS, v2.0)
* Mockup: `m-14-tb-case-prototype.html` (the M-04 shell, TB profile)

## Dependencies / reuse

* **Profile of** M-04 Case Workbench (OGC-790) — reuses Case/Isolate/AST-Run/Timeline/reports.
* **Needs** M-02 WHO-TB critical-concentration breakpoint extension (OGC-787).
* **Feeds** M-09 WHONET-TB export extension (OGC-794).
* Routing decided by M-03 `workflow_type` (OGC-789).

## Sizing

\~89 story points (XL profile work + 2 new entities + molecular capture + staged reports + DST). Sub-stories slice into: workflow_type routing; tb_smear; culture/day-N TB timeline; species ID; critical-concentration DST on micro_ast_run; tb_molecular_result + GeneXpert/LPA capture; MDR/XDR derivation; staged interim reports; critical handling.

## Status

One of the M-\* bundle epics; promoted into scope to satisfy procurement requirement #8 (Microbiology _and_ Mycobacteriology case workbench). /specify + mockup complete; awaiting sprint decomposition into child Stories.

fields.description:
## Overview

Get each lab's finalized AMR + TB results to **WHO GLASS** without breaking OpenELIS single-tenancy. OE's job is only to **transform and push its own finalized results** as FHIR (`DiagnosticReport` + per-drug `Observation`s, WHO AMR reporting profiles) to a **consolidated FHIR server**; that central server — the only place that sees all labs — does cross-lab first-isolate dedup and **generates the GLASS submission** (and a WHONET extract for an NCC that prefers files). Multi-tenant aggregation stays **outside OE**, consistent with `project_no_multitenancy`.

This is **complementary to**, not a replacement for, the M-09 WHONET file path: labs/NCCs that submit by WHONET file keep doing so; the FHIR path is the continuous, standards-based alternative that feeds the same central aggregator.

## Reuse-first (verified against OpenELIS-Global develop @ d7435687)

* `FhirTransformService` already builds `DiagnosticReport` + `Observation` (`transformResultToDiagnosticReport(Analysis)`) — extend it with the AMR-profile transform.
* `FhirPersistanceService.createFhirResourcesInFhirStore(map)` + `FhirConfig` — reuse for the push/endpoint.
* `EQAFhirSubmissionService.submitResultsViaFhir(...)` (1 DiagnosticReport + N Observations, scoped by organization) — the established pattern to follow for `MicroSurveillanceFhirSubmissionService`.
* `fhir_uuid UUID` column convention (AGENTS.md) — add to `micro_case` / `micro_isolate` / `micro_ast_run`.
* **M-09** first-isolate dedup, validation, run-history, scheduling; **M-02** breakpoint snapshots; **M-01** coded masters — all reused. No new transport, result store, or vocabulary.

## Scope

**Phase 2+ — the LAST module in the bundle.** Build only after M-04/M-05 (bacterial), M-14 (TB), M-09 (WHONET), and M-02 (breakpoints incl. WHO-TB) have shipped, since M-15 transforms and pushes exactly their finalized output.

* AMR FHIR transform (extend `FhirTransformService`): DiagnosticReport + organism Observation + per-antibiotic AST Observations with interpretation, raw MIC/zone, method, and M-02 breakpoint snapshot.
* `MicroSurveillanceFhirSubmissionService` (EQA pattern) + `surveillance_submission_run` audit (mirrors `whonet_export_run`) + `fhir_uuid` on three micro entities.
* Trigger modes: on-finalize / scheduled / manual.
* Validation reuse (M-09): block on unmapped codes with inline "Map now".
* GLASS minimum (de-identified) dataset only.
* TB via `workflow_type = MYCOBACTERIOLOGY_TB`: R/S-at-critical-concentration, molecular flags, MDR/pre-XDR/XDR category.
* Config + run/history surfaces (`/admin/surveillance/fhir`, `/reports/surveillance-submission`).
* Central aggregation + GLASS generation documented as **out of OE scope**.

## Source documents

* `m-15-glass-fhir-surveillance.md` (consolidated FRS, v1.0)

## Dependencies

* **Blocked by** M-09 WHONET (OGC-794), M-14 TB (OGC-901), M-02 breakpoints (OGC-787); reuses M-04/M-05 (OGC-790/791).

## Sizing

Final epic of the M-\* bundle; satisfies the GLASS-reporting portion of procurement requirement #8. /specify complete; awaiting sprint decomposition.

fields.description:
## Summary

The tech-facing escape hatch when a case's `workflow_type` is missing or wrong. Normally `workflow_type` is set automatically from the ordered test (M-03 §2.1a), but an untyped/mis-typed culture test, or a combined order, can leave a case `UNASSIGNED` or in the wrong profile. The bench tech needs a single, audited way to move it to the correct workflow.

**Parent epic:** OGC-790 (M-04 Case Workbench). **FRS:** M-04 §4.9.

## Behavior

* New classification state `UNASSIGNED`: case created without a valid `workflow_type` (untyped test or manual Program fallback edge) shows an amber "Needs workflow" chip in the header + Worklist flag; profile-dependent bench work (AST setup, breakpoint family, report templates) is held until classified.
* **Change workflow** control in the case header → inline panel (Principle 3, no modal): Workflow type select (Bacteriology / Mycobacteriology–TB) + required reason + culture-protocol Method picker (pre-filled with the chosen workflow's default Method).
* Confirming re-instantiates the case **profile** (M-04 ↔ M-14 sections), **breakpoint family** (CLSI/EUCAST ↔ WHO-TB, M-02), **organism vocabulary** (M-01), reflex variant, and **WHONET flavor** (M-09); writes a classification transition + Timeline note (reuse History/Note: who/when/from→to/reason); clears the chip.

## Guards

* Free while early (no isolates worked / no interpretive results).
* Once an isolate is identified or AST/DST results exist → warn that reclassifying detaches profile-specific results (bacterial AST vs TB DST differ); explicit confirm required; incompatible results retained + flagged, never silently deleted.
* Blocked after final report release (use amendment path).
* Permission reuses `micro.case.edit` (no new key).

## Acceptance criteria

* \[ \] A case with no valid `workflow_type` is `UNASSIGNED` with header chip + Worklist flag; profile-dependent actions held.
* \[ \] Change workflow expands inline; sets/changes `workflow_type`; pre-fills the default Method; requires a reason.
* \[ \] Reclassification swaps profile/breakpoint family/organism vocab/reflex/WHONET flavor and writes an audited Timeline note.
* \[ \] Early cases reclassify freely; cases with results warn + require confirm + retain incompatible results; released cases are blocked.

## Dependencies

* Relates M-03 trigger resolver (OGC-789) and the Test Catalog workflow attribute story.
* Relates M-14 TB profile (OGC-901) — this is how a case enters/leaves the TB profile.

## Size

M.

[WILL NOT FIX: superseded by OGC-1383] Microbiology: "Final release ready" but Release final report stays disabled (patient-report mapping missing)
fields.description:
**Found by:** Casey, on https://amr.openelis-global.org, case 26PHML00003L (`b7c94607-2ec0-49a2-a3cd-f9f3c11c277f`, Urines, Bacteriology, stage PRELIM_RELEASED). Verified with the case's own REST responses.

## What happens

The workflow is complete and the Reports section shows **"Final release ready ✓"** with no blockers, but **Release final report** is disabled. Nothing on the page says why, except a small grey tag under the preview: "Patient-report mapping required for final release".

## What the server returns for this case

* `GET /rest/microbiology/cases/{id}/readiness` → `finalReleaseReady: true`, `blockers: []`
* `GET /rest/microbiology/cases/{id}/release/preview` → `reportableContent: true`, `mappingConfigured: false`, `projectedResultIds: []`

## Cause

* `ReportReadinessPanel.jsx` enables the button only when `readiness.finalReleaseReady && projection.reportableContent && projection.mappingConfigured`. The readiness service (`MicroCaseReadinessServiceImpl`) never checks the mapping, so it can report "ready" while the button stays off.
* `mappingConfigured` (`MicroReportProjectionServiceImpl.hasReportConfiguration`) needs every `micro_case_analysis` link to have a `reportable_test_analyte_id`, and the test must have an active REMARK test result.
* The link copies `reportable_test_analyte_id` from the culture setup **when the case is created** (`MicroCaseAnalysisServiceImpl.linkAnalysis`). This case used culture setup "Bacteriology" (method 53, Plate Culturing), which has no reportable analyte. The two UAT setups (methods 52 and 54) have one, which is why UAT cases release.
* Fixing the setup later does not repair existing cases: `linkAnalysis` returns the existing link unchanged.

## Expected

1. Readiness reports the mapping (and reportable content) as blockers, with plain wording and the test or setup to fix. "Final release ready" is never shown while release is impossible.
2. Existing cases pick up a corrected culture setup mapping (re-resolve at preview/release, or backfill), so a stuck case can be released without database work.
3. Case 26PHML00003L can be final-released once the setup is fixed.

## Related

Culture setup admin has no way to set the reportable analyte: see the linked ticket.

**Found while diagnosing OGC-1384** on https://amr.openelis-global.org.

## What happens

`GET /rest/microbiology/admin/reference/culture-setups` on the AMR server:

* "Bacteriology" (method 53, Plate Culturing): **no** `reportableTestAnalyteId`
* "UAT bacteriology culture" (52) and "UAT alternate bacteriology culture" (54): have one (e.g. 294). These came from the UAT scenario seeding, not the admin screen.

Every case made under a setup without a reportable analyte has `mappingConfigured: false` and can never be final-released (OGC-1384).

## Cause

* The culture setup form definition (`frontend/src/components/admin/microbiologyReference/definitions.js`) offers method, name, workflow, media, incubation, subculture, max days, atmosphere and active, but **not the reportable test analyte**. The API accepts `reportableTestAnalyteId` (`MicroCultureSetupAdminForm`), and only the configuration loader and the UAT scenario set it.
* **Likely, not yet confirmed:** `saveCultureSetup` sets `reportableTestAnalyteId` from the request with `trimToNull`, so saving an existing setup from the admin form (which does not send the field) may clear it. Editing the UAT setups in the UI could break their release too.

## Expected

1. The culture setup form lets an admin choose the reportable test and analyte. Pick from reportable analytes of the test, and check that the test has an active REMARK result type, or explain why it can't be used.
2. Saving the form never clears a field the form does not show.
3. The setup list shows which setups are not ready to release reports.

fields.summary: Microbiology AST worklist: the default month uses the browser's time zone, but the server filters by its own
fields.description:
## What happens

The AST worklist defaults to the current month. The browser works out that month in its own time zone and sends plain dates; the server compares each row's collection date in the JVM's time zone. When the two zones differ, results collected near a month boundary fall outside the default view.

* `frontend/src/components/microbiology/MicrobiologyRoutes.js:84-98`: `getWhonetDateRange("THIS_MONTH", now)` (`WhonetRoutes.js:35-46`) builds `from`/`to` from `now.getFullYear()`/`now.getMonth()`, which are browser-local.
* `src/main/java/org/openelisglobal/microbiology/service/MicroWorklistServiceImpl.java:343-349`: `row.collectionDate.toLocalDateTime().toLocalDate()` is compared with those dates in the server's zone.

Example: a lab whose server runs on East Africa Time and a user whose browser is on UTC. At 21:30 UTC on 30 September, the browser asks for 1 to 30 September; a sample collected that minute is dated 1 October on the server and is filtered out.

## Effect on CI

`frontend/playwright/tests/foundational/harness/microbiology-analyzer-ast.spec.ts:47` (`expect(row).toBeVisible()`) fails in the last three UTC hours of each month. The CI browser runs in UTC and the harness webapp runs `TZ: Africa/Nairobi` (`projects/analyzer-harness/docker-compose.base.yml:53`). Every failing run on `develop` commit `3f42f5615d` started between 21:22 and 22:42 UTC on 2026-09-30. #4495 failed the same assertion that evening and passed on rerun.

## Fix

* Product: derive the default window from the server's date (or send the browser's zone with the request) so both sides agree on "this month".
* Test: open the worklist on a range that contains the seeded collection date instead of relying on the default window.

**Found on** https://amr.openelis-global.org, case 26PHML00003L, Reports section (same case as OGC-1384).

## 1. WHONET readiness shows the wrong label

The WHONET box heading says "WHONET export ready", but its check line says **"✓ Final release ready"**. `ReportReadinessPanel.renderReadinessItems` always uses `microbiology.readiness.ready` for the ready row, for both boxes. Expected: the WHONET row uses a WHONET message (e.g. `microbiology.whonet.ready`), with the key added to `en.json`.

## 2. Patient report text contains what looks like an ID

The patient report preview reads: `ISO-1: Klebsiella pneumoniae; Ciprofloxacin d0d3be0a2 R` (same content in `release/preview`). "d0d3be0a2" looks like a code or ID fragment in the antibiotic name. Please check:

* whether the antibiotic record on that server is simply named that way (test data), or
* whether the report builder adds a code or ID to the antibiotic name.

If it's the builder, the patient report should show the antibiotic's display name only.

fields.summary: Microbiology v2: bench-driven cases without declared workflows (tests added at each stage, computable incubation, incoming results)
fields.description:
### What the lab user is trying to do

A microbiology technician decides at the bench what a specimen needs: a Gram stain, an AFB smear, a GeneXpert, a culture, a DST panel. Today OpenELIS makes each culture test declare a workflow (Bacteriology or TB) and a culture setup in advance. When that is missing or wrong the case lands Unassigned and has to be reclassified. Direct microscopy has no home, incubation is free text so nothing tells the bench a plate is due, and a small site cannot refer the rest of the work and get results back on the same case. This feedback comes from the CPHL Port Moresby workflow breakdown.

### What we're building

* **No declared workflow.** Program = Microbiology opens one case per specimen per lab unit. The lab unit is chosen at order entry and can be changed later. What makes a case TB or bacteriology is the tests and panels on it.
* **Case details move to the Case view** (clinical history, prior antibiotics, TB history), with required fields clearly marked.
* **New case sections:** Initial testing (microscopy, wet prep, Gram, GeneXpert, with an option for a previous report), a referral point, Growth work-up (internal-only exams, subcultures), Additional testing (for example WGS).
* **Add any test or panel** from the catalog at each stage; reflex rules still add tests on their own.
* **Computable incubation:** a number plus a unit per inoculation, check reminders, a dated read log, and a Needs attention worklist filter.
* **Incoming results:** analyzer or referral results with no matching row wait for a tech to place them.
* **Report choice per result**, plus a reversible In lab only flag.

### How it fits the lab workflow

Reception picks the Program and lab unit. Everything else happens on `/microbiology/case/:caseId`, and the Worklist (`/microbiology/worklist?status=attention`) shows what is due.

### What it touches in OpenELIS

Much of this is **rework of code on develop**: `workflow_type`, culture setups, the routing resolver and the Change workflow panel are retired. It also touches the order entry Microbiology section, the Case view, the Worklist, analyzer result placement, referral returns and report selection. Every reversal of the V1 specs is boxed "Contradicts V1" in the document.

### Links

* [Gallery entry](https://digi-uw.github.io/openelis-work/#/microbiology/microbiology-v2-amendments)
* [Standalone HTML preview](https://digi-uw.github.io/openelis-work/designs/microbiology/amr-micro-v2-preview.html)
* [v2 amendments document (impact summary, A-01 to A-15, acceptance criteria)](https://github.com/DIGI-UW/openelis-work/blob/main/designs/microbiology/amr-micro-v2-amendments.md)
* Environmental follow-on: OGC-1382 ([gallery](https://digi-uw.github.io/openelis-work/#/microbiology/m-18-environmental-microbiology))
* No slicing guide yet; the developer slices, starting from the impact summary.

### Out of scope

* Micro QC (media and stain lots, ATCC controls) and isolate storage, flagged as gaps
* Breakpoint content changes

**Documentation:** a Feature Doc child is expected when this reaches In Review.

fields.summary: Environmental Microbiology: cultures for swabs, water and food with a site instead of a patient (M-18)
fields.description:
### What the lab user is trying to do

A microbiology lab receives environmental samples as well as patient samples: ward surface swabs from infection prevention, cooling-tower water, food from a complaint. Today the only way to culture them is to invent a fake patient ("Ward 3 Environment"), which then shows up in patient searches, the antibiogram, WHONET and GLASS. Culture tests also sit on the ordinary Results screen as "Not started" for days, inviting entry outside the Microbiology Case.

### What we're building

* A separate **Environmental Microbiology** lab unit. Lab units keep one domain, and staff who work both benches get both units.
* Environmental Microbiology Cases that use the same Case as patient cultures, with a **sampling site and sampling point** as the subject. Purpose (routine monitoring, post-cleaning check, outbreak investigation, complaint) and replicates are recorded on the Case.
* Culture tests worked only in the Case, never on Results or Validation. This also fixes clinical cultures.
* Environmental isolates kept out of the antibiogram and GLASS, and sent to WHONET only by an explicit choice, coded as environmental. Outbreak-investigation swabs are not counted by cluster detection.

### How it fits the lab workflow

Reception picks Program = Microbiology on an environmental order and a lab unit for each culture sample (`/order/environmental/enter`). The bench works the Case at `/microbiology/case/:caseId` on the Microbiology v2 layout, and sees patient and site rows together on `/microbiology/worklist`.

### What it touches in OpenELIS

Results and Validation worklists, environmental order entry, the Microbiology Case and Worklist, the culture purpose code list, WHONET export, and the cluster detection environmental stream. No schema change of its own; the Case routing and lab unit keying come from Microbiology v2.

### Links

* [Gallery prototype](https://digi-uw.github.io/openelis-work/#/microbiology/m-18-environmental-microbiology)
* [Standalone HTML preview](https://digi-uw.github.io/openelis-work/designs/microbiology/m-18-environmental-microbiology.html)
* [FRS v0.5](https://github.com/DIGI-UW/openelis-work/blob/main/designs/microbiology/m-18-environmental-microbiology.md)
* [JSX mockup source](https://github.com/DIGI-UW/openelis-work/blob/main/designs/microbiology/m-18-environmental-microbiology.jsx)
* [Slicing guide (6 slices, suggested)](https://github.com/DIGI-UW/openelis-work/blob/main/designs/microbiology/m-18-environmental-microbiology-breakdown.md)
* [Analysis report](https://github.com/DIGI-UW/openelis-work/blob/main/designs/microbiology/m-18-environmental-microbiology-analyze.md)
* Depends on: [Microbiology v2 amendments (gallery)](https://digi-uw.github.io/openelis-work/#/microbiology/microbiology-v2-amendments), [v2 document](https://github.com/DIGI-UW/openelis-work/blob/main/designs/microbiology/amr-micro-v2-amendments.md)

### Out of scope

* Vector cultures and food-specific enumeration methods
* Linking environmental samples to a cluster investigation (with M-16)
* Choosing a ward directly as the site, until Locations & Organizations lands

**Documentation:** a Feature Doc child is expected when this reaches In Review; the manual entry is written at Acceptance from verified behaviour.
